# @codenhub/store

> Small typed records persisted to key-value backends. One typed object per storage key, with whole-object reads and writes. The package and driver contracts are experimental.

Use for small records with last-write-wins semantics. Queries, transactions, and cross-process coordination belong in a database. Stores clone state; failed driver reads skip read-modify-write writes, while parse and validation failures can be overwritten with fallback plus changes. Recoverable failures use `store.*` events reported only through the store's `onError`; callback exceptions propagate. `storeErrors` provides optional user-facing registry feedback for every `StoreErrorCode`.

Node.js requires version 24 or newer. Portable values must survive a JSON round-trip. Only sync stores have a default (localStorage) driver. Cloudflare KV can return stale reads even after writes and permits about one write per key per second; prefer Durable Objects for read-modify-write.

## Documentation

- [Documentation overview](docs/index.md): Scope, requirements, guarantees boundary, and reading path.
- [Core stores](docs/core-stores.md): Sync and async methods, snapshots, validation, every error code, and failure handling.
- [Storage drivers](docs/storage-drivers.md): JSON portability, browser, memory, atomic single-process Node files, Cloudflare limits, and custom drivers.
